posts.text:
Jack Ma told Elon Musk humans will always be smarter than machines. 

Musk’s reaction says everything.

“Computers may be very clever, but human beings are much smarter. We invented the computer. I've never seen a computer invent a human being.”

Ma's argument was simple. Computers are tools. They calculate faster, remember more, but humans still hold something machines don't: experience, judgment, wisdom.

Musk clearly didn't buy it. “What would be an example of something that humans are better than a computer at?”

Watching this exchange now feels completely different than it did then. AI agents aren't just calculating anymore. They're writing code, analyzing documents, planning tasks, deciding what to do next on their own.

METR found that the length of software tasks frontier agents can complete autonomously has historically doubled roughly every seven months, with signs of even faster progress through parts of 2024.

That's where Ma's argument starts to buckle. For decades, technology automated what humans did. AI is starting to automate what we assumed required a human to think.

And companies were already learning to create enormous value with almost no people before this wave even arrived. Instagram sold for $1 billion with 13 employees. WhatsApp sold for $19 billion with 55.

Now picture what happens when a small team can direct hundreds of machines that never sleep, never take a salary, never need an office.

The question was never just which jobs disappear.

It's what happens to the money once fewer humans are needed to create it in the first place.

That's the question behind 2028: The Economy Without Humans.

Who gets the money when machines do the work?

quote.author: Rothmus
quote.name: Rothmus 🏴
quote.text:
A humanoid is a capital good on a scale that changes the constraint. It lengthens production and raises what labor and land can turn out, which is the abundance Elon is pointing at.

A person supplies about 2,000 hours a year. A robot on a 168 hour week supplies about 8,700. His floor of 1 billion within 10 years, priced in the low 10,000s, equals about 4 billion full time equivalents against a world labor force of 3.5 billion. 
The 10 billion at 15 years is an order of magnitude past that. 

Robots building robots still require saving, because energy, materials, and machines have to be bid into that line.
Expected abundance holds for ordinary wants which is what matters for people as consumers. Housing, food, care, and routine medicine get repriced toward energy and materials until a household’s budget stops being what limits them. 

An owner running 100s or 1,000s of agents earns the return on that capital stock, which is also how universal high income shows up as purchasing power. 

Money prices remain the way to allocate whatever is still scarce, that is energy, locations, raw materials. At least in the short term. 

Energy is the binding input, and settling more than one planet adds land, minerals, and generation beyond a single world.

TLDR: (1) More energy. (2) Multiplanetary doesn’t hurt.

Elon Musk explains why Tesla is being extremely careful while scaling Robotaxi

The ambition is massive...but Elon’s priority is making sure they do not hurt anyone

There are roughly 30,000–40,000 automotive deaths every year in the U.S., and most receive almost no national attention

But if a Tesla Robotaxi injures even ONE person, it can instantly become worldwide headline news and regulators could clamp down on the entire operation

So Tesla has to do two things at the same time:

Scale Robotaxi as fast as humanly possible

AND make sure it causes essentially no harm

Elon put it very simply:

“We do not want to injure anyone”

“And ideally...not even run over a pet”

That is the real constraint on Robotaxi right now

And despite being this cautious, the rollout is accelerating fast

Tesla’s authorized Cybercab fleet in Texas has nearly QUADRUPLED in just one month

45 → 169 Cybercabs

And Tesla now has 589 Robotaxi vehicles authorized in Texas when you include 420 Model Ys

Unsupervised Robotaxi miles have also been growing at double-digit rates week after week

So Tesla is not moving slowly

It’s scaling incredibly fast while trying to maintain an insanely high safety bar

That’s the balance Elon is trying to solve https://x.com/XFreeze/status/2080096187584274809/video/1

posts.text:
Falcon 9 flew more missions in ONE YEAR than the entire Space Shuttle program flew in 30 years

• The entire Shuttle fleet:
135 missions from 1981–2011

• Falcon 9 in 2025 alone:
165 launches

SpaceX exceeded the Shuttle program’s entire lifetime mission count by 30 launches in just 12 months

And Falcon 9 also launched more times than every other orbital launch vehicle combined that year

At the Shuttle program’s historical average cadence, reaching 165 missions would have taken roughly 37 years

Falcon 9 did it in ONE

And the hardware reuse comparison is just as insane:

• Space Shuttle Discovery — 39 flights across roughly 27 years
• Falcon 9 booster B1067 — 37 flights in just over 5 years

B1067 first flew on June 3, 2021

By August 25, 2026, the same booster had launched and landed successfully 37 times

A single Falcon 9 first stage came within TWO flights of the most-flown Shuttle orbiter’s lifetime flight count in about one-fifth of the time

What once took decades of launch operations now happens within a single year of Falcon 9 cadence

SpaceX turned reusability into an industrial-scale operation

When Lauren Friedman showed up at Amherst College, she was surprised to discover that almost every single girl in her dorm and on her athletic team was already taking SSRIs.

Inside jokes about Zoloft & Lexapro were common on campus, and everyone seemed deeply grateful their persistent anxiety and depression from teenage years was magically disappearing from a pharmaceutical drug.

Like her peers, @lololizzle had struggled earlier in life with both anxiety and depression -- so Zoloft seemed like a perfect solution. After all, all of her friends were taking it too, so how bad could it be?

Little did she know, SSRIs are causing a silent epidemic among Gen Zers called Post-SSRI Sexual Dysfunction, or PSSD. Like untold tens of thousands of other people just like her, Lauren now has completely lost her libido, sensation in her genitals, and even a sense of emotional connection with the people around her... PERMANENTLY.

She says she and others like her were NEVER given informed consent about the risk of developing PSSD, and American doctors will rarely even diagnose the condition at all.

Whether it's birth control being thrown in the faces of teenage girls to magically "regulate your hormones" or Zoloft instantly prescribed to "make you happy," one thing is clear--the young women of Generation Z are being poisoned en masse without any understanding of what may happen to them down the line.

it’s honestly insane how much of the modern tech tree has been unlocked because of a single guy

- next generation tunneling
- reusable rockets
-global satellite internet
- basically the modern space industry
- Moon and Mars transportation

- frontier AI
- gigantic AI supercomputers
- physical world AI

and the wildest part is that these branches are now starting to merge

there is a very real chance that this one guy ends up being the reason humanity reaches Kardashev II

genuinely the man of the millennium

quote.author: OwenSparks
quote.name: Owen Sparks
quote.text:
For those not aware, NASA certified the Cybertruck as an Astronaut Emergency Egress Vehicle, allowing SpaceX to replace their aging MRAPs.

If something goes wrong on the pad, the crew needs to get as far away as possible, as quickly as possible, and Cybertruck provides that speed and protection.

A NASA spokesperson said that both the agency and SpaceX "assessed the capability of the vehicle for all situations that would be encountered in an emergency and found that the Cybertruck met NASA’s requirements."
